content:
Apple has raised the price of Apple Music subscriptions in the US and other countries today. Starting today, the Apple Music Individual plan will cost $11.99 per month, up from $10.99.

Apple has also raised the price of some Apple One bundles.

In response to a query from 9to5Mac, Apple said: "Due to an increase in licensing costs, Apple Music is raising the price of subscriptions starting today."

Apple Music and Apple One are getting more expensive

Here are the new monthly prices for Apple Music and Apple One starting today:

Apple Music

  • Individual: $11.99 (previously $10.99)
  • Family: $19.99 (previously $16.99)
  • Student: $6.99 (previously $5.99)

Apple One

  • Individual: $19.95 (unchanged)
  • Family: $27.95 (previously $25.95)
  • Premier: $39.95 (previously $37.95)

Before this Apple Music price hike, Spotify announced a round of price increases earlier, which Apple mocked on social media at the time. But even after this increase, Apple Music is still cheaper than Spotify.

This is the first Apple Music price increase in nearly four years. Apple's last price increase was in October 2022, when Apple Music's Individual plan went from $9.99 to $10.99 per month. Apple also raised the price of Apple One at that time.

Apple raised the price of Apple TV, Apple Arcade, and Apple News+ in October 2023, and the related Apple One bundles also went up in price.

Apple TV raised prices again in August 2025, but Apple One's pricing remained the same.
